title: fix(router): remove dvine.video from owned-domain allow-list
body:
## Summary
- `dvine.video` is **not** a divine-owned domain, but `classify_host` and `is_public_divine_host` treated it as one
- removes the allow-list entry from both functions, plus the tests and README copy that referenced it
- only `divine.video` and `dvines.org` remain as owned apex domains

## Motivation
Spotted while reviewing #8. With `dvine.video` in the allow-list, anyone able to point that domain (or a subdomain of it) at this Fastly service could have the router serve username lookups, NIP-05 responses, and well-known cache bypasses as if it were ours.

## Validation
- `cargo test --locked` — 42 tests pass

## Test plan
- [ ] confirm `divine.video` and `dvines.org` traffic is unchanged
- [ ] confirm `dvine.video` (if it ever resolves here) falls through to the not-our-domain `Apex` branch

title: fix(router): bypass cache for public well-known paths
body:
## Summary
- force public `/.well-known/*` requests to bypass Fastly cache at the router layer
- keep username-hosted `/.well-known/nostr.json` behavior unchanged
- add tests covering the public bypass and username/non-well-known exclusions

## Motivation
- external app and universal-link verification files on `divine.video` and `www.divine.video` were still serving stale cached 404s after the `divine-web` deploy fixes
- those requests traverse `divine-router` first, so the router must not cache public `/.well-known/*` responses

Related Issue: divinevideo/divine-mobile#3843

## Validation
- `cargo +1.93.0 test --locked`

## Manual Validation
- after deploy, verify:
  - `https://divine.video/.well-known/apple-app-site-association`
  - `https://www.divine.video/.well-known/apple-app-site-association`
  - `https://divine.video/.well-known/assetlinks.json`
  - `https://www.divine.video/.well-known/assetlinks.json`
  all return `200` with JSON content types
- confirm username NIP-05 still works at `https://<username>.divine.video/.well-known/nostr.json?name=_`

title: fix: preserve api publish forwarding at edge
body:
## Summary
- keep Fastly edge caching on `api.divine.video` only and leave `relay.divine.video` as the uncached backup path
- preserve `X-Forwarded-Host` and `X-Forwarded-Proto` when proxying Funnelcake API traffic through Fastly
- add unit coverage for relay uncached behavior and preserved forwarded headers for `api.divine.video`

## Why
`POST https://api.divine.video/api/events` needs to proxy through Fastly to `relay.divine.video` without losing the original host/proto that NIP-98 verification depends on. This makes the edge behavior explicit and tested.

## Verification
- `cargo +stable fmt --check`
- `cargo +stable test -- --nocapture`

title: fix: route invite.divine.video to invite-faucet backend
body:
## Summary
- Add `invite` to `SYSTEM_SUBDOMAINS` in the router so it's not treated as a username
- Route `invite.divine.video` traffic to the `invite_service` backend (`adversely-polished-yak.edgecompute.app`)
- Add `invite_faucet` backend config in `fastly.toml`

## Root cause
The wildcard `*.divine.video` domain on the router service was classifying `invite` as a username subdomain, returning `@invite not found` HTML instead of routing to the invite-faucet Compute service.

## Test plan
- [x] 27/27 unit tests pass (including new `test_classify_host_invite_subdomain`)
- [x] Wasm build succeeds
- [x] Deployed to production and verified:
  - `GET /v1/client-config` → 200 JSON with CORS headers
  - `OPTIONS /v1/validate` → 204 with proper preflight headers
  - `POST /v1/validate` → 200 JSON with CORS headers
  - Unknown routes → 404 JSON (not HTML)

> **Note:** Already deployed to production (v25) and verified working. This PR is for record-keeping — commits are already on `main`.

title: feat: ATProto handle resolution + expanded system subdomains
body:
## Summary

- Adds `atproto_did` and `atproto_state` fields to `UsernameData` struct (backward compatible via `#[serde(default)]`)
- Adds `/.well-known/atproto-did` handler for username subdomains
  - Returns `200 text/plain` with bare DID when `status=active`, `atproto_state=ready`, `atproto_did` present
  - Returns `404` otherwise
- Expands system subdomains: `names`, `login`, `pds`, `feed`, `labeler`
- Adds 11 new tests (ATProto resolution logic, JSON deserialization, new subdomains)
- NIP-05 (`.well-known/nostr.json`) behavior unchanged

**Companion PR:** divine-name-server publishes the ATProto fields to Fastly KV that this router consumes.

## Protocol

```
GET https://alice.divine.video/.well-known/atproto-did
→ 200 text/plain "did:plc:abc123..."  (if active + ready)
→ 404                                  (otherwise)
```

Users use `did:plc` identities. The DID document must claim the handle via `alsoKnownAs: ["at://alice.divine.video"]` (PDS operator responsibility).

## Test plan

- [x] All 26 cargo tests pass
- [ ] Deploy and verify `/.well-known/atproto-did` returns 404 for users without ATProto state
- [ ] After divine-name-server sets ATProto state, verify resolution returns the DID
- [ ] Verify NIP-05 still works
- [ ] Verify system subdomains (names, login, pds, feed, labeler) passthrough correctly

title: fix: NIP-05 subdomain lookup uses correct username
body:
## Summary

Fixes NIP-05 verification for subdomain identifiers like `_@daniel.divine.video`.

**The bug:** When querying `daniel.divine.video/.well-known/nostr.json?name=_`, the code was looking up `"_"` in the KV store instead of `"daniel"`, returning an empty response.

**The fix:** Always look up the subdomain username in KV, but return the queried name in the response per NIP-05 spec.

## NIP-05 Spec Compliance

Per NIP-05, `_@daniel.divine.video` should:
1. Query `daniel.divine.video/.well-known/nostr.json?name=_`
2. Return `{ "names": { "_": "pubkey" } }`

Now supports both identifier formats:
- `_@daniel.divine.video` (underscore convention for root identity)
- `daniel@daniel.divine.video` (explicit username)

## Test plan

- [x] Added 16 unit tests covering:
  - NIP-05 response building (underscore, username, relays, not found, inactive, case insensitivity)
  - Host classification (apex, system subdomains, user subdomains, multi-level)
  - hex-to-npub conversion
- [x] All tests pass (`cargo test`)
- [x] No clippy warnings (`cargo clippy --all-targets`)
